bugs.text: centerText called without a scale passes undefined to textW, giving NaN x, so all scale-1 centred text is never drawn: HIGH SCORE (HUD and title), PRESS ENTER TO START, READY, NUMBER OF HITS/BONUS/PERFECT, the game-over SHOTS/HITS/RATIO results and PRESS ENTER. Confirmed by screenshots.
Challenge stage skips wave 0 (wave incremented before the first spawn), so only 4 waves/32 enemies appear and the 10,000 PERFECT bonus (total===40) can never be awarded.
Entry groups never use zako slots 8,9,18,19: only 36 enemies per normal stage instead of 40.
Stage badges wrong: one badge whose value is d[stage-1] (stage 2 shows 5), stage 7+ shows (stage-5) badges of 50.
Boss/escort group id never cleared, so a boss later diving alone (or re-entering) can still score 800/1600 if old escorts are alive.
Hit statistics reset each stage, shotsFired over-counts (adds total shots on screen), challenge kills and non-lethal boss hits not counted.
Ramming with a dual fighter destroys both halves instead of one.
If the boss is killed while the captive is still flying to it, the captive attaches to the dead boss object and is held forever (state 'gone' is never set), blocking future captures.
'/' not in the font, so the score table reads '50 100', '150 400 800 1600'.

summary: A compact, well-organised clone with a proper fixed-timestep loop, clean pixel sprites with wing flaps, a coloured twinkling starfield, curved group entries, sway/breathing formation, curved dives with escorts, and a complete tractor-beam / capture / rescue / dual-fighter chain that traces correctly in code. Its biggest flaw is a one-line helper bug: centerText without a scale yields NaN coordinates, so every small centred message (HIGH SCORE, PRESS ENTER TO START, READY, challenge results, the whole game-over hit-ratio screen) is invisible, which the screenshots confirm. The challenge stage spawns only 4 of 5 waves so PERFECT is unreachable, the formation is 36 enemies rather than 40, and stage badges do not follow arcade counting. Core shooting play works and feels recognisably like Galaga, but the missing text and rule errors make it noticeably rough.
